primitives.meaning: a reviewer identifying a specific fact the decision turns on and which is not available
entryFilters: a reviewer identifying a specific fact the decision turns on and which is not available
no instance of this journey is already open for the the decision case and the specific information requirement blocking it
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

primitives.does: Specify the exact requirement - which fact, which document, from whom, and why the decision needs it. A vague request produces a vague answer and a second round; and asking for unrelated things in case they help turns one gap into a questionnaire, which is how a two-day case becomes a three-week one

Record AWAITING_INFORMATION and preserve everything the review has already established. The case is paused rather than reset - more information required is not a rejection, and a reviewer returning to it should not be starting again from the beginning

primitives.asks: Who actually holds the outstanding information?

branches.label: The requester or another external party
branches.test: only someone outside the organisation can supply it

branches.label: Someone inside the organisation
branches.test: an internal owner, team or system holds it, or is the one authorised to produce it

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it

primitives.purpose: Request what is still outstanding from the external source, naming it precisely.
primitives.brief: Request what is still outstanding from the external source, naming it precisely. Re-requesting the whole requirement asks for things already given, which reads as the first submission having been ignored - and asking a customer for something an internal system already holds is the most common version of this failure
primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

primitives.does: Raise the outstanding requirement as owned work against the internal holder, carrying the blocked decision and its unchanged deadline. An internal evidence gap routed down a customer channel asks the wrong party on a route they never agreed to

primitives.reads: the the decision case and the specific information requirement blocking it re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

branches.label: Information arrived
branches.test: something was supplied against the requirement

branches.label: The decision is no longer required
branches.test: the request was withdrawn or the thing it was about no longer exists

primitives.does: Record the case as no longer requiring a decision, with the reason. This is not a rejection and not an approval, and reporting it as either tells the requester something untrue about what happened

primitives.state: no longer requiring a decision; the review history stands unclosed rather than concluded
primitives.reEntry: a renewed need for the same judgment is a new request, which can reference this case and its evidence

primitives.does: Validate what arrived for relevance and completeness against the stated requirement. Something arriving is not the requirement being met - a document of the right type saying the wrong thing satisfies a checklist and not a decision

primitives.asks: Does what arrived satisfy the requirement?

branches.label: It does
branches.test: the requirement is met, relevantly and completely

branches.label: Partly
branches.test: some of the requirement is met and some is not

primitives.asks: Does policy allow requesting the remainder?

branches.label: It does, within the request budget
branches.test: further rounds are permitted and the case has not used them all

branches.label: It does not, or the budget is exhausted
branches.test: no further round is permitted, or the case has already been round-tripped as often as the model allows

primitives.does: Apply the timeout semantics policy defines - escalation, closure, or a decision on the evidence available. Which one applies comes from policy: a case that quietly closes because nobody answered is a rejection nobody made, and a case that quietly proceeds is a decision made on evidence somebody knew was incomplete

primitives.asks: What does policy define for an expired information deadline?

branches.label: Decide on what is available
branches.test: policy permits deciding on the evidence in hand, with the gap recorded as a gap

branches.label: Close the case
branches.test: policy explicitly closes an unanswered case, with defined semantics for doing so

branches.label: Escalate, or policy does not define it
branches.test: policy escalates - or says nothing, in which case no closure semantics are invented here

primitives.does: Close the case under the semantics policy actually states, recording that it closed for want of information rather than on its merits

primitives.state: closed for want of information; no decision was made on the merits
primitives.reEntry: a new request with the information present is assessed fresh, and this closure does not count against it

primitives.on: an information deadline expiring with escalation or with no defined closure semantics
carries: the requirement, what was and was not supplied, and the review already done
the explicit fact that no closure or rejection was invented to end the case

primitives.on: an information requirement resolved, or exhausted under policy
carries: what was supplied and what remains missing, stated as a gap rather than smoothed over
the full prior review history, so the reviewer continues rather than restarts
